extracted.intended_audience: K08 review committee members, grant reviewers, and mentors evaluating a mentored clinical scientist research proposal in tuberculosis immunology
extracted.subtask_description: A mentored clinical scientist (K08) Research Strategy describing aims, hypotheses, experimental designs, expected results, potential pitfalls, statistical justification, biosafety and training plans for mechanistic studies of antibody-mediated macrophage control of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence that Fc/FcR engagement mediates intracellular Mtb restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that intact antibody Fc and FcR engagement are required for observed effects on intracellular Mtb by enzymatically separating F(ab)2 and Fc and by deglycosylating IgG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate F(ab)2 and Fc via IdeS cleavage and purify fragments; cleave glycans with PNGase. Test F(ab)2, Fc, and combined fractions, and deglycosylated IgG in the in vitro macrophage infection model and compare bacterial burden to intact Abs. Expectation: enzymatic manipulation that prevents Fc–FcR interaction should abrogate Fc effector effects. If effects persist with F(ab)2 or deglycosylated IgG, consider Fc-independent mechanisms (e.g., cytokine neutralization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for implicating FcγRIIIa specifically
rubrics_metrics.description: Localized clustering and colocalization of IgG with FcγRIIIa, and functional loss of effect upon targeted knockdown of FcγRIIIa but not inhibitory FcγRIIb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualize co-localization/clustering using fluorescently labeled IgG and anti-FcγRIIIa staining; perform targeted siRNA knockdown of FcγRIIIa and, as a control, FcγRIIb. After knockdown, infect macrophages and measure bacterial burden. Expected: FcγRIIIa knockdown (but not FcγRIIb knockdown) should abrogate the IgG-mediated effect. Also expect enhanced FcγRIIIa clustering at the membrane and enhanced colocalization with LTB vs ATB IgG if FcγRIIIa is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and causal linkage between inflammasome/IL-1β and phagolysosomal fusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that inflammasome activation and IL-1β production precede and are necessary/sufficient for enhanced phagolysosomal fusion and decreased bacterial burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform kinetics (6, 24, 48, 72, 96 h) measuring IL-1β (ELISA) and ASC specks alongside lysosomal co-localization. Test sufficiency with recombinant IL-1β and nigericin (inflammasome activator) and necessity with neutralizing anti-IL-1β and inflammasome inhibitors (MCC950, beta-hydroxybutyrate, glyburide). Expected results: inflammasome activation/IL-1β should occur prior to phagolysosomal fusion; exogenous IL-1β/nigericin should drive fusion and reduce bacterial burden; antagonists should abrogate these effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autophagy involvement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify autophagy/autophagolysosome markers co-localizing with Mtb and test whether autophagy is required for antibody-mediated bacterial restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stain for LC3 and p62 and use autophagy-specific dyes; use rapamycin as a positive control. Co-stain with Lysotracker to assess acidic vesicles. Validate contribution by applying autophagy blockers (3-methyladenine or wortmannin) or siRNA knockdown of autophagy components and assess whether these interventions abrogate antibody effects on bacterial burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental infection model standards (in vitro macrophage assay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use primary human monocyte-derived macrophages infected at low multiplicity (MOI 1) with virulent H37Rv Mtb-MCherry, wash away extracellular bacteria, then co-culture with antibodies and assess intracellular bacterial burden by fluorescence microscopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix and image after specified timepoints (e.g., 96 h) and analyze via high-throughput microscopy and CellProfiler. Use THP1 as an alternative cell system if primary macrophage manipulations (e.g., siRNA) activate macrophages non-specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and positive/negative comparators in assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate controls such as pooled IgG from LTB and ATB individuals, healthy control sigma IgG, no antibody, positive activators (nigericin, rapamycin), and technical controls (PNGase, IdeS treatments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use positive controls (nigericin for inflammasome, rapamycin for autophagy) and negative or baseline comparators to interpret directionality (enhanced restriction vs enhancement of replication) and to ensure specificity of observed phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative imaging and phagocytosis scoring methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure bacterial burden and phagolysosomal co-localization by high-throughput fluorescence microscopy and quantitative image analysis (CellProfiler); generate phagocytic scores for ADCP using flow cytometry-derived MFI and percent frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute phagocytic scores as function of mean fluorescence intensity and percent frequency. Use appropriate staining (Lysotracker, ASC, LC3, p62) and ensure replicate wells. Statistical tests described in manuscript: Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed rank test, and Student t-test as appropriate for comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of molecular perturbations to test necessity and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ siRNA knockdown and small-molecule inhibitors to probe necessity of specific receptors/pathways (e.g., FcγRIIIa, inflammasome, autophagy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: siRNA against FcγRIIIa and FcγRIIb (control) in primary macrophages or THP1 cells; small-molecule inhibitors MCC950, BHB, glyburide for inflammasome; 3-methyladenine/wortmannin for autophagy. Be aware of potential off-target activation (siRNA-induced activation) and have alternative strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive criteria for alternative mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider that F(ab)2 fragments or deglycosylated IgG may still mediate effects via Fc-independent mechanisms such as cytokine neutralization or other effector functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enzymatic manipulation does not eliminate activity, investigate non-Fc mediated mechanisms (e.g., neutralization), broaden discovery approaches (RNAseq) to identify unexpected pathways, and avoid overattribution to Fc/FcR without multiple lines of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and sample size justification for antibody-feature discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Power calculations based on preliminary cohorts and feature-wise effects to determine cohort sizes and significance thresholds for multiple testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using preliminary data (partial correlation ~0.50 for top features), 68 individuals (34 LTB, 34 ATB) gives 80% power at alpha 0.0005 (Bonferroni-Holm correction for 100 features). Plan to increase to 40 LTB and 40 ATB to improve power. Provide explicit effect size estimates and rationale tied to multiple-testing correction strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use linear regression controlling for covariates (e.g., age) to calculate p-values and adjust for multiple comparisons using methods appropriate for dependency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform linear regression with covariate adjustment; use Benjamini and Yekutieli method to control false discovery under dependency. Engage biostatistics support (MGH Biostatistics Center) for analysis and power/sample-size calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and regulatory compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct all M. tuberculosis laboratory work in approved BSL3 facilities and comply with institutional and federal biosafety guidelines and approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in BSL3 at Harvard School of Public Health or Ragon Institute under institutional IBC approvals; follow CDC BMBL guidance and NIH recombinant DNA guidelines. Serum handling and cell culture in BSL2 with selected BSL3 practices. Ensure personnel training, competency demonstration for BSL3, and medical clearance prior to unescorted access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and update RCR certifications and participate in institutional RCR training appropriate to career development awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possess CITI certifications and Partners RCR seminar (4-hour seminar + four 1-hour hospital courses), and plan to take Harvard Catalyst RCR course (2 hr/week for 8 weeks). Discuss RCR topics biannually with Training Advisory Group and in weekly mentor meetings; document ongoing RCR engagement and updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship, training, and time-allocation standards for a mentored career development award
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define mentor commitments, meeting frequency, advisory committee structure, access to resources, and trainee time allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors commit to weekly meetings (decreasing over time but at least monthly), biannual advisory committee meetings, annual evaluations, and provision of resources, cores and career guidance. Trainee time allocation: ~75% research, <15% clinical duties, ~50 hours/year teaching. Plans for manuscript milestones and grant submissions (R21 in Year 4, R01 in Year 5) should be articulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and deliverables expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a multi-year timeline matching aims to years and specify expected manuscripts and grant-submission milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map aims to Years 1–5, list anticipated manuscripts (one per year in Years 2–4), additional pilot studies, R21 preparation in Years 3–4, and R01 preparation in Years 4–5. Demonstrate feasibility of completing the proposed work within the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential pitfalls identification and alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate experimental limitations (e.g., siRNA-induced macrophage activation) and provide alternative strategies (e.g., use THP1 cell line, broaden discovery with RNAseq).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state likely technical or interpretive pitfalls and concrete alternatives to address them (different cell systems, use of orthogonal assays, broader unbiased approaches such as RNAseq) to strengthen the likelihood of interpretable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of orthogonal assays and multiple lines of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine imaging, biochemical (ELISA), genetic (siRNA), enzymatic, and pharmacologic perturbations to support mechanistic claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triangulate findings by showing concordant results across different modalities (e.g., imaging co-localization, ELISA IL-1β readouts, functional bacterial-burden assays after genetic or pharmacologic perturbations) to robustly infer mechanism and causality.
